item.title: Jazz Brunch w/ “Four Peanuts” trio — Sat Nov 14, 11:30 AM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
Jazz Brunch is now officially on the schedule for every Saturday here in the taproom! We’re so very excited to introduce our newest free weekly event, open to all ages, family & pet-friendly
If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!
We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Signup opens Sunday Nov. 15th at 8:00 PM]**
We'll hop onto the beautiful Mountains-to-Sea Trail and head south for a simple out-and-back, a relatively mild 3 miles each way. We'll do a 15-minute break at the turnaround point.
Dogs are welcome, but they must be leashed per Forest Service regulations.
**MEETING TIME & DIRECTIONS**
We'll gather at 9:00 AM on the south side of the **Fresh Market parking lot** in front of the **Haywood Appliance** store. The address is 1378 Hendersonville Rd. Look for me at my silver Hyundai.
Link for Google Maps: [Fresh Market Parking Lot](https://maps.app.goo.gl/VBNrrBeuUSnLeU3j6)
We'll set out by **9:05**.

item.title: Fun & easy way to play more tennis (please read event description for details) — Thu Dec 3, 7:00 PM
item.description:
PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis We’re still working to get more people into these Meetups, but our goal is to give PlayYourCourt members a few social tennis outings each week in addition to your practice sessions and Challenge League matches.
These Meetups are co-ed, super laid back, and all skill levels are welcome. Post your skill level and a suggested court in the comments section so we can round up as many players as we can for some tennis fun!
Also, if you’re looking to meet new practice partners or play some matches and you aren’t already in the PlayYourCourt Community, you can go here to see what we’re all about and sign up:
https://www.playyourcourt.com/tennis-community/asheville-nc/meetup/
If you love tennis, we’d love to have you! Be sure and watch the quick video that explains how everything works.
Happy hitting!
- Scott
Source: PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis

Being present for ourselves is a significant challenge that often creates a gap. This gap represents the difference between the way we aspire to live and how we actually live. We choose to bridge this gap because it is the right thing to do.
Introducing a great way for new nomads to connect and discover important key takeaways for their lives. As a new Asheville Digital Nomad, where do you go if you don’t know many people?

The trail is a 7.5 mile rails-to-trails partnership between the City of Easley and the City of Pickens. We will be start at the Pickens trailhead, walk 3 miles, and return to the start point. We will be sharing the trail with bikers, runners, and rollerbladers.
Local residents nicknamed the railroad the "Pickens Doodle" line, because the freight engine could not be turned around and had to run backwards from Easley to Pickens, looking like a doodlebug.
Pickens Doodle Park, where the trailhead is located, includes restroom facilities, a railroad depot museum, a pavilion, benches, bike racks, and a train-themed playground.

item.title: Listening through the Seasons: Introduction to Soundscapes — Fri Jan 8, 1:00 PM
item.description: Listening through the Seasons: Introduction to Soundscapes with Meg Worthington Friday, January 8 | 1 – 3:30 pm BRN – Elective Register Here! How does the Arboretum sound in winter? What can we learn by listening closely? Join us as we launch a yearlong exploration of the NC Arboretum’s changing soundscape. In this introductory session, participants will discover the field of soundscape ecology, learn how scientists use sound to study ecosystems, and practice techniques for deep listening and observation. Together, we’ll visit our first listening station, collect baseline observations, and begin documenting the sounds of winter. Listening Through the Seasons is a yearlong community science and soundscape ecology project at the NC Arboretum. Participants will help document the changing sounds of the Arboretum throughout the year while learning about ecology, biodiversity, and the art of deep listening.
